title: Recovery options pocket guide for tenants (incident comms) - 2029-03-10
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, customer-facing recovery-options pocket guide we can use during inference-impact incidents. The audience is: account teams, on-call CS leads, and the on-call SRE/Eng tech writer who needs to assemble a short status page + a follow-up customer postmortem summary.

Notes to self
- Keep the public statuspage text < 220 words unless a partner needs more details.
- Give customers 2–3 clear choices (opt-in) when we offer replay/rollback or evidence packages.
- Use plain language; avoid infra jargon in the top section; include a technical appendix for enterprise customers.
- Include a short verification checklist customers can run (self-serve) and an assurance lane for enterprise customers that want Redwood-performed verification.

Quick TL;DR template (status page opening paragraph)
- Investigating: "We are investigating increased latency and occasional incorrect responses for text-generation requests in the eu-west-1 region. Some requests are seeing delayed streaming and truncated structured outputs. We’re working to identify the root cause and will update within 30 minutes."
- Mitigated/Partial: "We have applied a routing change reducing impacted requests by ~85% for most customers. Some tenants may still see degraded responses; we are offering an opt-in replay and verification package. ETA for full resolution: 24–48 hours."
- Resolved: "Service is restored to normal operating levels. We’ve implemented a mitigation and are completing a customer-facing review; details and optional verification steps are below."

Customer choice menu (compact, three lanes)
1) Self-serve verification + lightweight replay (recommended for most):
   - We provide a filtered evidence bundle (sample request/response pairs, timestamps, tenant IDs truncated) and a short checklist customers can run to confirm data integrity. No action required from Redwood unless customer requests a replay.
   - Pros: fast, minimal disruption. Cons: requires customer to run checks.

2) Redwood-managed verification + selective replay (recommended for enterprise tenants with bounded traffic):
   - Redwood will run verification for a customer-provided window and offer to re-run affected requests using pinned model versions. Customer consents to Redwood replaying requests or tokens. Replay is rate-limited and scheduled to avoid upstream spikes.
   - Prospectus to ask for: confirmation of tenant IDs, earliest/ latest timestamp, and a communication lead for pairing.

3) No replay, mitigations only (opt-out):
   - Customer chooses not to participate in replay. Redwood will provide a signed evidence pack and a short technical summary for audit logs.

Opt-in form copy (short)
- Subject: Request for Redwood-managed verification and replay
- Body: "I confirm tenant <TENANT-ID> would like Redwood to run verification for the window <START> to <END> and to replay affected requests as needed. Contact: <NAME, EMAIL, PHONE>"

Statuspage snippets (short variants)
- Investigating (one-liner for status page grid): "Investigating higher latency and truncated outputs in eu-west-1. Engineering triage in progress."
- Partial mitigation (bullet for details): "Traffic has been rerouted; ~85% reduction in symptoms. Some queued requests may be processed slowly — using 'Safe Mode' routing for sensitive tenants."
- Resolution (final): "Full service restored. Post-incident customer summary forthcoming. If you want Redwood-managed verification, please opt in using the template above."

Customer postmortem (1–2 page customer summary outline)
1) Executive summary (3–4 sentences)
   - What happened (plain language), which tenants/regions were affected, severity (S1/S2), duration, and customer-facing impact (latency, truncated outputs, missing streaming chunks).
2) What we found (concise root cause)
   - Short summary: e.g., "A routing configuration change triggered cascading prefix-cache invalidations in the inference runtime; under burst conditions this caused KV cache thrashing and a subset of streaming sessions to truncate."
3) Impacted customers & scope
   - List affected regions, approximate % of requests, and guidance on how to check if a tenant was affected (checklist).
4) Immediate mitigations we applied
   - Routing rollback, temporary rate-window, pin-to-stable-model policy, burst-queue drain.
5) Customer-facing remedies offered
   - Evidence bundle, Redwood-managed verification & replay, compensatory credits (if applicable), and timeline for replay completion.
6) Permanent fixes and timeline
   - Config validation guard, additional canary layer for routing changes, KV-cache instrumentation improvements, rollout of automated rollback on cache-eviction anomalies. ETA: planned in two sprints; expected production rollout in four weeks.
7) How customers can verify (self-serve checklist)
   - Steps: 1) identify request window, 2) export request IDs using your SDK logs (example command), 3) run the sample diff script we provide, 4) file opt-in if you want Redwood to perform a replay.

Evidence bundle contents (what we will attach)
- Redacted request/response samples (<= 500 rows)
- Service logs with timestamps (redacted PII)
- Model and runtime versions pinned during the window
- Audit trail of routing and config changes
- Short reproduction script (dev-only) for trusted customers

Tone and apology language (brief)
- Opening: "We sincerely apologize for the disruption and the impact to your service. This does not meet the reliability levels we aim to provide."
- Accountability line: "We own this impact and are prioritizing customers that were most affected for verification and remediation."

Operator checklist for CS on-call (quick)
- Pick the lane (1/2/3) with the customer in the first 90 minutes.
- If customer picks lane 2, collect: tenant-id, earliest/latest timestamps, contact person, and consent line. Upload consent to JIRA ticket JIRA-OPS-3421.
- Schedule Redwood replay only in low-traffic windows (customer preference).
- Communicate ETA for replay and final closure within 72 hours of consent.

Appendix — example self-serve verification commands (for internal use)
- Example: sdk logs export --tenant <TID> --from <START> --to <END> --format jsonl > customer-window.jsonl
- diff-script usage: python verify_responses.py --redwood evidence.jsonl --customer customer-window.jsonl

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm standard SLAs for replay window length across tiers (how far back do we allow a replay without special approval?).
- Decide template language for credits (flat credit vs. pro-rated usage credit) and escalate to Finance for final wording.
- Finish the enterprise appendix: legal/consent language and KMS/HSM handling for on-prem private deployments.

Draft snippets to copy into final status page or customer email
- Short apology and action: "We're very sorry — a runtime routing change caused some customers in eu-west-1 to receive truncated and delayed responses. We rolled back the change and mitigated ~85% of traffic impact. If you'd like us to replay requests from <START> to <END>, reply with the opt-in template above and we will prioritize verification for your tenant."

End of doc

(Working doc — keep concise; share with SRE and product for wording sign-off before customer send.)
